Northern betacism (Cintra's all-Northern trait 1), realised strongly in Braga: the /v/ ~ /b/ opposition is lost and both merge into a single phoneme /b/, surfacing as the stop [b] or the softer spirant [β] (vou -> [bow], vaca -> [ˈbakɐ], vacina -> [bɐˈsinɐ]). Cintra (1971:87): 'o desaparecimento da oposição fonológica entre os fonemas /v/ e /b/ e a sua fusão num fonema único /b/, realizado ora como oclusiva, ora como fricativa (ou espirante) b ou β' — the [β] variant is recorded in the allophones inventory. NATIVE ATTESTATION: the Braga speaker Miguel in Portuguese With Leo, 'Sotaque e expressões de Braga' (native-speaker source, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xaen3F8256M): 'pões o B em vez do V ... muitos sons que em português standard seriam Vvvv, mas vocês dizem um B ... às vezes é um B mais pronunciado, outras vezes é um B mais suave tipo Bou' (vou -> bou); and 'no norte diz-se bácina, às vezes assim com um ligeiro B' (vacina). Modelled as a post-lexical phoneme-side rewrite so the merger applies uniformly however /v/ arises from the inherited grapheme map.

Diphthongisation of the tonic CLOSE-mid front vowel [e] -> rising [je] (mês -> [ˈmjeʃ], ele -> [ˈjelɨ]), the diagnostic diphthongisation of the Baixo-Minho / Douro-Litoral zone (of which Braga, in the Minho, is part). Cintra (1971): 'a ditongação, tão caracterizadora, das vogais tónicas fechadas [e] em [je], [o] em [wo]'; Segura (2013) names diphthongisation of stressed vowels the characteristic trait of the north-western variety. NATIVE ATTESTATION: the 8-accents overview (Portuguese With Leo, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pitj0XxYO7I) records the Braga 'o quê' -> 'o quiê' (insertion of the [j] onglide: quê [ke] -> [kje]) and 'mieu' (meu). Gated to the CLOSE [e] only (genuinely open tonic [ɛ] does NOT diphthongise); same pre-lexical open/close LIMIT as pt-PT-x-porto — words whose standard value is close [e] but which the base engine transcribes [ɛ] (cedo, medo) escape the rule, which is deliberately not widened to [ɛ]. Brissos (2018; Brissos & Rodrigues 2016) shows the OPEN mids diphthongize too — see the companion *_DIPHTHONGISE_E_OPEN/_O_OPEN rules; the earlier 'genuinely open [ɛ]/[ɔ] does NOT diphthongise' caution is superseded by that stronger acoustic source.

Diphthongisation of the tonic CLOSE-mid back vowel [o] -> rising [wo] (avô -> [ɐˈbwo], pôr -> [ˈpwoɾ]), the back-vowel counterpart of BRA_DIPHTHONGISE_E in the same Cintra (1971) Baixo-Minho passage; Segura (2013). Gated to CLOSE [o]; genuinely open tonic [ɔ] does not diphthongise. Same pre-lexical open/close LIMIT as pt-PT-x-porto. Brissos (2018; Brissos & Rodrigues 2016) shows the OPEN mids diphthongize too — see the companion *_DIPHTHONGISE_E_OPEN/_O_OPEN rules; the earlier 'genuinely open [ɛ]/[ɔ] does NOT diphthongise' caution is superseded by that stronger acoustic source.

Diphthongisation of the tonic OPEN-mid front vowel: stressed open [ɛ] -> rising [jɛ] (pé -> [ˈpjɛ], café -> [kɐˈfjɛ]). Brissos (2018, pp.196-197, 200-201; reporting Brissos & Rodrigues 2016, AVOC + ALEPG/ALE) overturns the earlier close-mid-only view: NW diphthongization applies to the open mids too ('[ˈpi̯ɛ] pé'), so that only the cardinal vowels stay phonologically stable. This also RESOLVES the open/close pre-lexical mis-selection that the close-only DIPHTHONGISE_E documented as a limit — whichever mid the base engine selects for a spelling-unmarked stressed <e>, it now diphthongizes (to [je] or [jɛ]). Restricted to the stressed nucleus. NOTES-ONLY (not modelled): the co-existing toward-central subtype RD2 ([ɛɐ̯]) and the marginal /i/->[ei̯].

Diphthongisation of the tonic OPEN-mid back vowel: stressed open [ɔ] -> rising [wɔ] (toque -> [ˈtwɔkɨ], só -> [ˈswɔ]; and the emblematic Porto, whose base-engine open [ɔ] now diphthongizes to [ˈpwɔɾtu], approaching the attested close [ˈpu̯oɾtu]). Brissos (2018, pp.196-197, 200-201; Brissos & Rodrigues 2016) — open mids diphthongize in the NW. Restricted to the stressed nucleus. NOTES-ONLY (not modelled): the co-existing toward-central subtype RD2 ([ɔɐ̯]) and the marginal /i/->[ei̯].

DISABLED here: this variety has its own productive stressed mid-vowel process (metaphony / diphthongisation) that owns the open/close realisation of the stressed vowel, so the inherited standard-language lexical open/close pins (PT_LEX_*) must not pre-empt it. The standard lexical list is a Lisbon/BP-standard fact; the open/close of stressed mid vowels under this dialect's own vowel system is documented residual.

Overridden for this northern variety: the nucleus is the close-mid [e], not the central [ɐ]. Matching it here, not disabling it, also keeps the stressed nucleus away from any tonic-[e] diphthongisation rule of the spec. Northern EP keeps the close-mid nucleus of word-final ⟨-em -ens⟩: [ẽj̃], [ẽj̃ʃ] (bem [ˈbẽj̃], homem [ˈɔmẽj̃], homens [ˈɔmẽj̃ʃ]). The centralised [ɐ̃j̃] of the pt-PT base is the Lisbon merger: Wikipedia 'Portuguese phonology', 'In Greater Lisbon, [ẽj̃] has merged with [ɐ̃j̃]'; Ciberdúvidas (Viana & Rocha 2006, 'Vogais e ditongos nasais, outra vez', n. 1): 'em dialectos do português europeu … a grafia -em/-en(s) representa o ditongo [ẽj̃]'. Leite de Vasconcellos 1901 (Esquisse d'une dialectologie portugaise, §44n, p. 93; quoted from an OCR copy, diacritics normalised): '-em < l. -ENE correspond -ẽ dans certains endroits de la frontière de Tras-os-Montes et du Minho, et -ẽi ou -ɐi dans le reste du pays'. The border monophthong [ẽ] is local and not modelled. The oral parallel in the same section (§44i): the diphthong ⟨ei⟩ is [ɐj] only 'à Lisbonne' and [ej] in Entre-Douro-e-Minho, the Beira and Trás-os-Montes. The rule matches ⟨m⟩ only, so word-final ⟨-en⟩ (hífen) is not matched here and falls to PT_FINAL_EN_NUCLEUS of pt-PT.
Overridden for this northern variety with PT_FINAL_EM_NUCLEUS: the nucleus of the plural ⟨-ens⟩ is the close-mid [e], so it is [ẽj̃ʃ]. The sources are under PT_FINAL_EM_NUCLEUS in this spec.

Restricted to POST-tonic syllables in the Minho. A pretonic ⟨en em⟩ before a consonant keeps the reduced vowel, nasalised: [ɨ̃] (pensar [pɨ̃ˈsaɾ], lembrar, pensamento, vender, tendência, entender [ẽtɨ̃ˈdeɾ]). Leite de Vasconcellos 1900 (Estudos de Philologia Mirandesa I, §76, p. 238): 'Este phenomeno é caracteristico da lingoagem do Alto- e Baixo-Minho; toda a gente culta d'estas regiões … diz usualmente lẹmbrar, tẹmporada, intẹndimento, pẹnsamento, vẹnder (ou mesmo bẹnder!), tẹndencia'; the ring below is 'e surdo (= ẹ) nasal' (p. 201, table b, 'Como na pronúncia do Minho, nas palavras pensar, tentar, lembrar'). He cites Dialectos interamnenses VI §3, IX §8-b and Gonçalves Vianna, Essai de phonétique, p. 46, n. A word-initial ⟨en em⟩ takes the base word_initial [e] and is not reduced. The post-tonic ⟨-em -ens⟩ still un-reduces, so homem stays [ˈɔmẽj̃].

Overridden for this variety: the close-mid vowel of a word-final ⟨-er⟩ infinitive takes the Baixo-Minho rising diphthong [je] (comer [kuˈmjeɾ], ter [ˈtjeɾ]), the same change as BRA_DIPHTHONGISE_E for every other stressed close [e]. Sources: Leite de Vasconcellos, Esquisse d'une dialectologie portugaise (1901), §44-b, p. 90 (OCR copy of archive.org esquissedunedia00vascgoog, diacritics normalised): 'l'ê oral ou nasalisé, et l'ê (em, en) initial ou médial deviennent iê dans le Baixo-Minho : piêra, tiêmpo, miênos'; Cintra (1971), as quoted in this spec: 'a ditongação, tão caracterizadora, das vogais tónicas fechadas [e] em [je]'. The vowel is close because Infopédia and Priberam give it so in standard European Portuguese (see PT_ER_CLOSE in pt-PT); before that rule existed the infinitive was the open [ɛ] and came out [ˈkuˈmjɛɾ]. The rule matches here, rather than being disabled, because the first matching rule fixes the surface and the diphthongisation rule would not run after it.

Overridden for this variety: the open-mid vowel of the ⟨-er⟩ nouns of PT_LEX_OPEN_ER in pt-PT takes the rising diphthong [jɛ] (mulher [muˈʎjɛɾ]), as every other stressed open [ɛ] does here (Brissos 2018, pp. 196-197, 200-201, as cited under the open diphthongisation rule of this spec). The rule matches here, rather than being disabled, for the same reason as PT_ER_CLOSE.

notes: Bracarense (Braga) European Portuguese — a Northern (Minho) variety of the Cintra Baixo-Minho / Douro-Litoral zone, described natively as HEAVIER / more strongly Northern than Porto (Portuguese With Leo, 'Sotaque e expressões de Braga', native-speaker source, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xaen3F8256M, and the 8-accents overview https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pitj0XxYO7I). A DELTA spec over the broad pt-PT base; it inherits the whole standard EP system (unstressed vowel reduction, dark coda /l/, coda-sibilant chiado, sandhi) and declares only the Northern deltas. MODELLED FEATURES: (1) BETACISM — /v/~/b/ merge in /b/ (~[β]) (allophone rule BRA_BETACISM), attested more categorically than Porto's variable merger: Miguel 'em Braga vai-me sair naturalmente trocar o V pelo B'. (2) TONIC-CLOSE-VOWEL DIPHTHONGISATION — [e]->[je], [o]->[wo] (BRA_DIPHTHONGISE_E/_O), the Cintra Baixo-Minho marker, natively attested via 'quiê' (quê) and 'mieu' (meu). (3) DIPHTHONG PRESERVATION — <ou>->[ow] (Miguel: 'tu dizes OU, dizes vOU ou bOU') and <ei>->[ej] kept where Lisbon monophthongises/lowers ([o], [ɐj]) (inherited-map grapheme deltas). NOT MODELLED (documented, not faked): (a) the northern 'vogais mais abertas' / prosodic lengthening for emphasis (Miguel: 'abres mais o A em cantÁdo ... prolongar algumas sílabas quando queremos dar uma ênfase especial') and the 'mais musical / mais cantado' cadence are gradient prosodic traits, not segmental rules. (b) The word-final paragogic /r/ release in -ar verbs (Miguel: 'vocês dizem tipo Faláre, gostarE ... a meio caminho entre o ehrr mais inglês e o ere mais certinho') is variable ('já não foi tanto') and hard to gate to infinitives orthographically; left inherited. (c) The 'beim' (bem) realisation is nasal-diphthong detail left to a downstream engine. (d) 'Vós ides / vinde / ide' is a morphosyntactic, not phonological, feature. LIMIT (shared with pt-PT-x-porto): the diphthongisation rules are gated to CLOSE mid vowels; because open/close for spelling-unmarked stressed <e>/<o> is lexical and the inherited pt-PT map defaults to the OPEN allophone, some underlying-close words (cedo, medo) escape diphthongisation — widening to the open vowels would wrongly diphthongise genuinely open tonic vowels (café, avó) and is rejected. The apico-alveolar coda sibilant (Cintra's primary North/South isogloss) is an articulatory distinction not simulable at the phoneme/orthography level. ACOUSTIC UPDATE (Brissos 2018; Brissos & Rodrigues 2016): the OPEN mids diphthongize too ([ɛ]->[jɛ], [ɔ]->[wɔ]); modelled as BRA_DIPHTHONGISE_E_OPEN/_O_OPEN. RD2 (toward-central) and the marginal /i/->[ei̯] left to notes. APICAL ⟨ss⟩: ⟨ss⟩ is declared apico-alveolar [s̺]. Cintra 1971 (read in the Instituto Camões CVC reprint, pp. 11-13) draws the main North/South isogloss on the sibilant of the graphemes s and ss: apico-alveolar in the North, predorsodental in the South. His southern limit of the apical runs from the Ria de Aveiro to the Mondego, which it crosses upstream of Coimbra, and on towards Castelo Branco. He places the Baixo-Minho, where Braga lies, north of that limit, in the group that keeps only the apico-alveolar sibilants. The other sibilant graphemes keep the inherited plain values; carrying the apical to ⟨s⟩, ⟨ç⟩, ⟨c⟩ and ⟨z⟩ is an open limit of this spec.

ancestors.notes: Standard (Lisbon-type) European Portuguese; Braga diverges by (strong) Northern betacism (v->b/β), tonic-close-vowel diphthongisation ([e]->[je], [o]->[wo]), and diphthong preservation (<ou>->[ow], <ei>->[ej]).

sources.author: Portuguese With Leo (with Miguel, bracarense)
sources.title: Sotaque e expressões de Braga
sources.notes: Native-speaker EP accent deep-dive (NOT academic). Attests, with example words: Northern betacism v->b/[β] ('pões o B em vez do V', 'vou/bou', 'vacina -> bácina, às vezes com um ligeiro B'); diphthong preservation <ou>->[ow] ('tu dizes OU, dizes vOU ou bOU'); more open vowels and prosodic lengthening ('abres mais o A em cantÁdo', 'mais musical, mais cantado'); and the variable word-final paragogic -r in -ar verbs ('Faláre', 'gostarE'). Braga framed as a distinct, heavier Northern accent.

sources.author: Portuguese With Leo
sources.title: The 8 Portuguese accents of Portugal
sources.notes: Native-speaker EP accent breakdown (NOT academic). Records the Braga tonic-close-vowel diphthongisation via 'o quê' -> 'o quiê' (quê [ke] -> [kje]) and 'mieu' (meu), and 'beim' (bem); grounds the BRA_DIPHTHONGISE_E reading together with Cintra's Baixo-Minho diphthongisation isogloss.

sources.author: Cintra, Luís F. Lindley
sources.title: Nova proposta de classificação dos dialectos galego-portugueses
sources.publisher: Boletim de Filologia (Centro de Estudos Filológicos, Lisboa), vol. 22, pp. 81-116
sources.notes: Foundational classification of the Galician-Portuguese dialect space. Trait 1 (betacism, p.87): 'o desaparecimento da oposição fonológica entre os fonemas /v/ e /b/ e a sua fusão num fonema único /b/, realizado ora como oclusiva, ora como fricativa (ou espirante) b ou β'. The Baixo-Minho / Douro-Litoral (of which Braga, in the Minho, is part) is delimited by 'a ditongação, tão caracterizadora, das vogais tónicas fechadas [e] em [je], [o] em [wo] (por vezes [wɔ])'. Grounds the modelled betacism and tonic-vowel diphthongisation.

sources.author: Segura, Luísa
sources.title: Variedades dialetais do português europeu
sources.publisher: In Raposo, E.B.P. et al. (eds.), Gramática do Português, vol. I, Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian, Lisboa, pp. 85-142
sources.notes: Modern EP dialectology synthesis. Names diphthongisation of stressed vowels as the characteristic trait of the north-western (Baixo-Minho / Douro-Litoral) variety and documents Northern betacism — the corroborating academic source for the Braga features modelled here.

sources.author: Mateus, M.H.M. & d'Andrade, E.
sources.title: The Phonology of Portuguese
sources.notes: Reference EP phonology for the inherited base processes (unstressed vowel reduction, dark coda /l/, coda sibilants) that Braga inherits unchanged from pt-PT.

sources.author: Brissos, Fernando
sources.title: Proposta de reformulação da caracterização dialetal do noroeste português
sources.publisher: Estudos de Lingüística Galega, Volume especial I: 193-208
sources.notes: Reformulates the diphthongizing 'variedade do noroeste' (Cintra's Baixo-Minho / Douro-Litoral), reporting AVOC + ALEPG/ALE data largely from Brissos & Rodrigues (2016). Central finding: tonic-vowel diphthongization is NOT limited to the CLOSE mids [e o] — it applies to the OPEN mids [ɛ ɔ] too ('[ˈpi̯ɛ] pé', '[ˈtu̯ɔkɨ] toque', pp.196-197, 200-201), so only the cardinal vowels stay phonologically stable; it also affects, marginally and contextually, the high front /i/ → [ei̯] ('[mɐˈkei̯ɐ] maquia', ~19% of tokens, pre-pause/vowel only, p.199). Two co-existing diphthong subtypes: within-axis (RD1: [i̯e i̯ɛ], [u̯o u̯ɔ]) and toward-central (RD2: [eɐ̯ ɛɐ̯], [oɐ̯ ɔɐ̯], pp.200-201). Grounds widening the diphthongization rules to the open mids; RD2 and the /i/-diphthong are documented but left unmodelled (co-existing variant / contextual).

sources.author: Brissos, Fernando & Celeste Rodrigues
sources.title: Vocalismo acentuado do Noroeste português — descrição acústica, variação dialectal e representação fonológica
sources.notes: The primary acoustic study behind Brissos (2018): AVOC formant data plus the dense ALEPG/ALE NW network. Argues the NW vowel systems require revising the close-mid-only diphthongization picture and that seven distinct vowel systems are needed to represent the continental dialects. Not open access; its examples and page-cited quadros are used here via the open-access Brissos (2018), which reproduces them.

stress.notes: Acordo Ortográfico 1990 conventions: paroxytone default; written accents override; final -i/-u/-r/-l/-z/-x/-im/-om/-um/-ins/-ons/-uns and nasal diphthongs attract final stress. Unmarked -em/-ens/-am stay paroxytone (homem, homens, falam): an oxytone of more than one syllable in -em or -ens is written with an acute (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base VIII, 1.º c: deténs, haréns, provéns, também). DIPHTHONGS: declared so the bundled syllabifier counts nuclei correctly — without them every vowel run merges into one nucleus and co-e-lho is read as coe-lho, one syllable short, putting the stress and its vowel reduction on the wrong vowel. ⟨oe⟩ is hiatus, not a diphthong (Cunha & Cintra, §Ditongos). COMPOUNDS: a hyphenated compound is one prosodic word. Each element keeps its own stress and the last is the strongest (Bechara, Moderna Gramática Portuguesa, p. 340, quoted in Ciberdúvidas, resposta 28042), so compound_stress is "last": guarda-chuva gwˌaɾdɐˈʃuvɐ (Portal da Língua Portuguesa). IPA_DIPHTHONGS is empty: the grapheme table writes every diphthong with a glide ([aj], [uj], [ɐ̃w̃]), so two full vowels side by side in the transcription are always a hiatus, and the stress mark is placed with each IPA vowel as a nucleus of its own. Read with the orthographic list, the IPA [ui] of ⟨proíbe⟩ /pɾuibɨ/ and [iu] of ⟨viúva⟩ merge into one syllable and the mark lands a syllable early. The acute on a tonic ⟨i u⟩ after a vowel marks exactly this hiatus (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base X, 1.º: juízes, ruína, ciúme, miúdo, saída, baú).
